tardoc.title: TARDOC compliance

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Everything doctors and hospitals ask before adopting DocNote. Still have a question?
faq.q1: What is DocNote and how does it work?
faq.a1: DocNote is an AI-powered medical scribe and clinical documentation assistant designed for doctors, surgeons, and hospitals in Switzerland, France, and across Europe. During a consultation, DocNote securely records the conversation between the physician and the patient, transcribes it in real time, and automatically generates a structured medical report (consultation note, discharge letter, operative report, ward-round note, etc.) that the doctor reviews and validates before sending to the patient's electronic health record.
faq.q2: Why choose DocNote over other AI medical scribes?
faq.a2: DocNote is built specifically for European and Swiss healthcare, not adapted from a US product. Key differentiators: (1) all data is hosted in Switzerland and never used to train AI models, (2) full compliance with the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP), GDPR, HIPAA, and ISO 27001, (3) automatic medical coding suggestions aligned with Swiss DRG and PMSI, (4) native TARDOC support to turn dictated exams into billable descriptions, (5) direct EHR integration with Mediway and SOKLE, (6) real synchronization between mobile and desktop, and (7) hospital-specific documentation including discharge letters, operative reports, and collaborative day-hospital files.
faq.a2Ch: DocNote is built specifically for Swiss healthcare, not adapted from a US product. Key differentiators: (1) all data is hosted in Switzerland and never used to train AI models, (2) full compliance with the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP / nLPD), HIPAA, and ISO 27001, (3) automatic medical coding suggestions aligned with Swiss DRG, (4) native TARDOC support to turn dictated exams into billable descriptions, (5) direct EHR integration with Mediway and SOKLE, (6) real synchronization between mobile and desktop, and (7) hospital-specific documentation including discharge letters, operative reports, and collaborative day-hospital files.
faq.a2Row: DocNote is built specifically for French and European healthcare, not adapted from a US product. Key differentiators: (1) all data is hosted in France and never used to train AI models, (2) full compliance with the European GDPR, HIPAA, and ISO 27001, (3) automatic medical coding suggestions aligned with the French PMSI, (4) direct EHR integration with leading hospital information systems, (5) real synchronization between mobile and desktop, and (6) hospital-specific documentation including discharge letters, operative reports, and collaborative day-hospital files.
faq.q3: Is DocNote secure and compliant with health data regulations?
faq.a3: Yes. DocNote applies end-to-end encryption (AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit), hosts all health data exclusively in Switzerland, and complies with the Swiss FADP, the European GDPR, HIPAA, and ISO 27001. DocNote acts as an auxiliary person to the physician under Article 321 of the Swiss Criminal Code (medical secrecy). Health data is automatically and irreversibly deleted within 7 days of processing. DocNote never retains permanent copies of audio, transcriptions, or medical reports.

DocNote applies end-to-end encryption (AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit), hosts all health data exclusively in Switzerland, and complies with the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP / nLPD), HIPAA, and ISO 27001. DocNote acts as an auxiliary person to the physician under Article 321 of the Swiss Criminal Code (medical secrecy). Health data is automatically and irreversibly deleted within 7 days of processing. DocNote never retains permanent copies of audio, transcriptions, or medical reports.
faq.a3Row: Yes. DocNote applies end-to-end encryption (AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit), hosts all health data exclusively in France in HDS-certified data centers (Hébergeur de Données de Santé), and complies with the European GDPR, HIPAA, and ISO 27001. DocNote is bound by French medical secrecy under Article 226-13 of the French Penal Code and Article L1110-4 of the Public Health Code. Health data is automatically and irreversibly deleted within 7 days of processing. DocNote never retains permanent copies of audio, transcriptions, or medical reports.
faq.q4: Which medical specialties does DocNote support?
faq.a4: DocNote covers 61 specialties across seven families — surgical, medical-surgical, medical, primary care, acute care, diagnostics, and allied health — with 227 templates and 10 cross-specialty documents. Coverage includes general practice, cardiology, surgery, gynecology, pediatrics, psychiatry, emergency medicine, intensive care, anesthesiology, radiology, dentistry, and many more. Templates use the vocabulary and structure expected for each specialty.
faq.a5: DocNote understands and produces reports in French, German, Italian, English, and over 20 other languages. It correctly handles Swiss-specific medical terminology and code-switching during consultations (for example a patient speaking Swiss German while the doctor dictates in French).
faq.q6: How much time does DocNote save per consultation?
faq.a6: On average, doctors using DocNote save more than 2 hours of administrative work per day. A consultation note that previously took 5 to 10 minutes to write is generated in seconds, leaving only a quick medical review before validation. This means more time with patients, fewer evenings spent on paperwork, and reduced burnout.
faq.q7: Does DocNote integrate with electronic health records (EHR)?
faq.a7: Yes. DocNote integrates directly with Mediway and SOKLE, with new EHR integrations regularly added. You can also drag and drop your own Word report templates: DocNote automatically recreates the report respecting your exact layout, then export to PDF or copy/paste into any other system.
faq.q8: How much does DocNote cost and is there a free trial?
faq.a8: DocNote offers a free trial of 30 consultations with full access to all professional features, with no credit card required. The Professional plan is CHF 109 per month (or CHF 99 per month billed yearly) for users in Switzerland, with equivalent pricing in EUR for the rest of Europe. Hospitals and large organizations have a custom Enterprise plan available on request.

The Professional plan is CHF 109 per month (or CHF 99 per month billed yearly). Hospitals and large organizations have a custom Enterprise plan available on request.
faq.a8Row: DocNote offers a free trial of 30 consultations with full access to all professional features, with no credit card required. The Professional plan is €89 per month (or €79 per month billed yearly). Hospitals and large organizations have a custom Enterprise plan available on request.
faq.q9: What makes DocNote different for hospital and day-hospital (HDJ) documentation?
faq.a9: DocNote is the first AI medical scribe purpose-built for hospital complexity, not just outpatient consultations. Three differentiators stand out. (1) Collaborative day-hospital files: in HDJ workflows where multiple caregivers (physicians, residents, nurses, anesthetists) successively see the same patient, DocNote lets every caregiver contribute to the same shared patient file and automatically merges all contributions into one structured, reliable, auditable record. No other ambient AI scribe on the European market currently offers this. (2) Rich consultation context: DocNote allows the physician to enrich any consultation by drag-and-dropping prior documents (lab results, imaging reports, prior discharge letters), attaching photos (wounds, lesions, ECGs, X-rays), or pasting free text. The AI then incorporates this rich context into the structured output, producing reports of unmatched precision. (3) Personal Word templates: drag and drop your own Word document with your exact formatting, signature, hospital letterhead, and section structure. DocNote recreates every future report respecting your exact template and layout. No other AI scribe offers this level of per-physician customization.

faq.q1: How does the free trial work?
faq.a1: Start with 30 free consultations with full access to Professional features. No credit card required.
faq.a2: Yes, you can upgrade or downgrade your plan at any time. Changes take effect at your next billing cycle.
faq.a3: Absolutely. All data is encrypted and stored in Switzerland. We are HIPAA compliant and ISO 27001 certified.
faq.q4: Which EHR systems do you integrate with?
faq.a4: We integrate with most major EHR systems including Epic, Cerner, and local Swiss systems like Sokle or Mediway.
faq.q5: What is the difference between Professional and Enterprise?
faq.a5: Professional is built for individual physicians and small practices: unlimited consultations, mobile and web access, templates, and priority support. Enterprise adds multi-user rollout, dedicated account management, custom EHR work, optional on-premise deployment, SLA, and structured training for hospitals and clinics.
faq.q6: Can I pay monthly or yearly?
faq.a6: Yes. You can choose monthly billing or yearly billing with about 15% savings. Prices are shown in your local currency when available (CHF, EUR, or USD).
faq.q7: Do you offer invoices for clinics and hospitals?
faq.a7: Yes. Professional subscriptions are billed through Stripe with downloadable invoices. Enterprise contracts can be invoiced through your procurement process with custom billing terms.
faq.q8: Is there a commitment or cancellation fee?
faq.a8: There is no long-term lock-in on the Professional plan. You can cancel before the next billing cycle. Enterprise agreements follow the terms defined in your contract.
faq.a9: Most solo clinicians start the same day after the free trial. Hospital and clinic rollouts usually take a few weeks depending on EHR integration, training schedule, and internal IT review.
faq.q10: Can multiple doctors in one practice share an account?
faq.a10: Small practices can start on Professional per clinician. For shared departments, admin roles, or hospital-wide access, the Enterprise plan is the right fit — contact sales and we will size it with you.

team.title: Designed by doctors, built by AI engineers
team.subtitle: A clinical and technical team working side by side to give physicians their time back.
team.intro: DocNote started in hospital corridors, not a pitch deck. Our founders still practice medicine, so every product decision is judged by whether it survives a busy ward round.
team.story: Today, clinicians, engineers, and go-to-market teammates share one mission: turn consultations into reliable clinical documents in seconds, with Swiss-hosted privacy at the core. We build with the people who will use the product tomorrow.
team.highlightsLead: DocNote did not start as a pitch deck. It started in hospital corridors — between ward rounds, operative lists, and evenings spent rewriting notes that should have written themselves. That origin still shapes every hire, every release, and every conversation we have with a clinic.

highlights.title: Practicing physicians at the core
highlights.body:
Our founders still practice medicine. That is not a slogan for the About page — it is the filter for product decisions. If a feature does not survive a busy ward round, a noisy emergency bay, or a Friday afternoon clinic, it does not ship.

Clinical language, specialty structure, and the real rhythm of hospital documentation come first. We design for discharge letters, operative reports, collaborative day-hospital files, and the awkward moments when three caregivers touch the same patient in one afternoon.

When clinicians tell us something feels wrong, we treat that as engineering input — not as a nice-to-have UX comment.

highlights.title: Swiss-hosted privacy by default
highlights.body:
Health data is not a training corpus. DocNote hosts clinical information in Switzerland, encrypts it in transit and at rest, and applies retention rules that match European expectations for medical secrecy.

We build for FADP / nLPD, GDPR, HIPAA, and ISO 27001 realities — hospital IT reviews, procurement questionnaires, and the quiet question every physician asks: where does my patient’s data actually live?

Nothing about ambient documentation is worth eroding trust. Privacy is part of the product architecture, not a legal appendix.

highlights.title: Clinicians and engineers in one loop
highlights.body:
Medical specialists, AI engineers, and product teammates sit in the same loop. Report models are not invented in isolation and then “adapted” for hospitals — they are co-designed with people who still write those reports by hand today.

That is why DocNote can move from free dictation to structured specialty notes, operative reports, follow-up notes, and discharge summaries without forcing doctors into a generic US outpatient template.

Engineering quality shows up as speed, reliability, and calm interfaces. Clinical quality shows up as vocabulary, structure, and respect for how care teams actually work.

highlights.title: From first demo to hospital rollout
highlights.body:
A good ambient scribe demo is easy. A trustworthy hospital rollout is not. Our sales, onboarding, and support teams help clinics map workflows, choose the right report models, connect EHR paths where needed, and train teams without interrupting care.

We stay through pilots, procurement, and the messy middle — specialty exceptions, template preferences, multilingual wards, and the IT checklist nobody puts in the marketing site.

The goal is simple: more time with patients, fewer evenings lost to notes, and a documentation system clinicians are willing to defend to their colleagues.

team.highlightsClosing: Today the team spans clinical leadership, deep engineering, go-to-market, and communication — united by one mission: turn consultations into reliable clinical documents in seconds, with Swiss-hosted privacy at the core. We build with the people who will use the product tomorrow.
